questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Legal prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates enough space in front of your vehicle for them to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through a flooded road. Water can hide many hazards, even if it looks shallow. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less effectively.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you slow down, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less effectively.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less effective your tires are at clearing water. If you go too fast, your tires lose their grip and you may hydroplane, or slide on water.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go. Once the vehicle starts to straighten, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a constant speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, maintain a steady speed. Do not increase your speed. Let the other vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, stay calm. Hold the steering wheel firmly and release the accelerator to slow down. Apply the brakes lightly once the vehicle has slowed. Move to the shoulder only after you have slowed considerably.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot potential hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic conditions. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles merging at on-ramps and expect rapid changes in road conditions.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective at clearing water from the road. If you drive too fast, your tires lose their grip and the vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving past a parked vehicle on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver may open the door as you approach. Use extra caution near parked vehicles.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Safe places to park your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Always look and listen for trains coming from either direction. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Human error.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or when drivers act unexpectedly. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You should:

options.text: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the vehicle's owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about what happened.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about hazards or special conditions ahead. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending ahead.
A divided highway is beginning ahead.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is beginning ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Keep traction by staying close to other vehicles.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Stay farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid sudden stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump them to slow or stop.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be extra careful on shaded roads under trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than sunny areas and take longer to dry.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving helps you:
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead to avoid sudden braking or turning. By looking ahead and being ready to stop or change lanes, you drive safer, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, you should:

options.text: Slow down and gradually return to the road when safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gradually return to the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Instead, reduce speed, check traffic, and gradually turn back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: While backing up, you should:

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Don't depend only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic signals are coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. You know right away that:

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: You can help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintaining a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed to help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance. Also signal when you turn, change lanes, or slow down.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. The best way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn on:
questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles or when other drivers cannot see you. Use low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see to the side, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly both ways.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop and inch forward until you can see in both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean stop. You must stop and give the right-of-way to other traffic. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, check:
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much more.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling next to the curb, but not when pulling away.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Signal when you pull next to a curb and when you pull away from a curb.
